findings.issue_text: [BUG] The immediateDelete=true branch of deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or marks the WorkflowReminder row, so a rescheduled/deleted booking leaves a permanently scheduled reminder row behind. On every reschedule (handleNewBooking) and step deletion (workflows.tsx), the old reminder row stays with scheduled=true and cancelled never set, so it is not picked up by the scheduleEmailReminders cron cleanup (which only processes cancelled=true rows); the row accumulates forever and every subsequent reschedule re-attempts a cancel against an already-cancelled batch_id, and scheduleWorkflowReminders' duplicate-suppression checks against these stale rows can suppress reminders for the new booking.

[BUG] The reminder cancellation calls in handleCancelBooking.forEach are unawaited async functions, replacing the previous awaited Promise.all batch, so the process can finish the handler before the SendGrid/Twilio calls and prisma deletes complete. In a serverless deployment the function freezes/exits after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` returns, killing in-flight deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder promises: the reminder rows are never marked cancelled or deleted and the SendGrid/Twilio cancel requests never fire, so cancelled bookings still receive reminder emails/SMS. The same unawaited pattern is repeated in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx (lines ~484-495) and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx (lines ~211-217, ~375-383, ~572-580).

[ADVISORY] The cron's cancel loop wraps all reminder cancels plus their prisma deletes in one try/catch that logs and continues, so a single SendGrid failure leaves the reminder row un-deleted and the cron retries the same cancel every run. One permanently failing referenceId (e.g. batch already cancelled) causes repeated cancel attempts on every cron invocation for up to the hour window; also a failure after the SendGrid call but before the delete leaves a cancelled row that gets a duplicate cancel POST next run. Additionally the sequential await of client.request per reminder makes the cron O(n) network calls in the reminder count.

[ADVISORY] PrismaPromise is now imported as a runtime value from @prisma/client after the only usage sites (the PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[] arrays) were deleted from this file, leaving the import unused. The unused import fails the repo's lint (no-unused-vars) in CI; if the workflow router is the last consumer, this is dead code that the next reader must reason about.

[ADVISORY] handleNewBooking now transitively imports smsReminderManager (and its Twilio client) and emailReminderManager (and its SendGrid client) into the booking-creation hot path, where previously only reminderScheduler was pulled in from that directory. Every booking request loads the Twilio/SendGrid SDK modules at module init even for bookings with no SMS/email workflows, increasing cold-start weight; if either manager module performs side-effectful client construction at import time, booking creation inherits a hard dependency on those service credentials being present.

[BUG] The phone-number section is now gated only on isPhoneNumberNeeded (the diff changes `{(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded) && (` to `{isPhoneNumberNeeded && (`), so a workflow step where isSenderIdNeeded is true but isPhoneNumberNeeded is false no longer renders the sendTo PhoneInput at all. Users with sender-id-requiring SMS configurations (verifiedNumbers path) lose the ability to enter/select a custom phone number for the step; the sendTo field and verify flow silently disappear, and the step cannot be configured as before. This is the sibling-flag miss on the touched rendering path: isSenderIdNeeded gates the same block but was dropped from the condition without a compensating branch.

[BUG] The try/catch around the reminder-cancellation forEach cannot catch anything: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async functions invoked without await inside forEach, so their returned promises are not observed by the catch. Any cancellation failure (SendGrid/Twilio error, Prisma delete failure) becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of hitting the log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders', error) the code was written for, and the reschedule continues with stale reminders that may still fire for the old booking time.

[BUG] The cron's cancellation loop makes one unguarded await per reminder inside a single try/catch: the first failing SendGrid call throws out of the for-loop, skipping both the SendGrid cancel and the DB delete for every remaining reminder, and the failed reminder is never deleted so it is re-fetched on every subsequent cron run. A single bad referenceId (e.g. batch already cancelled, SendGrid 4xx) permanently poisons the cancellation pass: later reminders within the hour window are never cancelled and send emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings, and the poisoned rows accumulate retries indefinitely. Error handling is console.log only, so nothing alerts or removes the poison row.

[BUG] The remindersToCancel query filters only on `cancelled: true` and scheduledDate, with no `method` or `scheduled` filter, so it can match reminders that were never actually scheduled with SendGrid (scheduled=false rows carry a referenceId but no SendGrid batch). Cancelling a booking while its reminder is still unscheduled marks the row cancelled:true (deleteScheduledEmailReminder sets cancelled without a SendGrid call in some paths, and rows created before scheduling exist); the cron then issues a SendGrid batch cancel with a batch_id that was never created, throwing and triggering the loop-abort failure above.

[ADVISORY] The new `cancelled` boolean column has no default (NULL for all existing rows) and no index, while the cron in scheduleEmailReminders.ts now scans WorkflowReminder for `cancelled: true` on every run. Every existing row matches neither true nor false explicitly, forcing developers to reason about three-valued logic in every future query on this column, and the hourly cron does an unindexed scan over the whole WorkflowReminder table as it grows with every booking.

[ADVISORY] The reminder-cancellation forEach fires async delete functions without awaiting them, and the removed `await Promise.all(...)` means cancellation of SendGrid/Twilio jobs and row deletion is not completed before the handler resolves; the old code's `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` guard was also dropped, so unscheduled rows now invoke deletion paths. The API response can return before remote cancellation jobs are dispatched, so a crash/process exit right after the response silently leaves reminders scheduled for a cancelled booking; unscheduled email reminders with a referenceId now set cancelled:true and rely entirely on the hourly cron instead of immediate cleanup.

[ADVISORY] Same fire-and-forget pattern as the other call sites: the reminder forEach invokes async delete functions with no await and the previous `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` barrier was deleted, and the `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` guard was dropped here too. Reschedule via tRPC returns before remote reminder cancellation completes (stale SMS/email may fire for the old slot on process exit), and unscheduled reminders now enter the cancelled-flag/cron path that was previously skipped, changing cleanup semantics for rows that were never sent to SendGrid/Twilio.

[BUG] The reschedule path cancels prior booking's reminders non-immediately (immediateDelete undefined for email), but nothing in the diff guarantees the new booking's reminders are distinct rows the cron can distinguish — while the workflows.tsx verifiedNumber/sender path change is not the issue here, the concrete gap is that no verification exists for any of the new cancellation behavior: the diff contains no test files at all (no spec/**, test/**, *.spec.*, *.test.* anywhere in the changed paths). The core acceptance criterion of the PR — reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings no longer fire — has zero verification: the new cancelled-flag cron path, the immediateDelete branch, and the referenceId=null early-delete branch are all untested, so a regression in any of them ships silently and manifests as users receiving reminders for bookings they cancelled.

[BUG] The try/catch around the reminder-cancellation forEach can never catch the async failures it claims to log, because deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async functions invoked without await inside a synchronous forEach, so rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections and the log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') branch is dead code. When SendGrid/Twilio cancellation fails during a reschedule, the operator-visible error log never fires, the reschedule proceeds believing reminders were cancelled, and the process emits an unhandled rejection that can crash the serverless invocation.

[BUG] Reminder cancellation is no longer included in the awaited Promise.all, so the cancel-booking handler returns (and in serverless the process freezes) while the SendGrid/Twilio cancel calls issued inside deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are still pending or have already failed silently via their internal console.log catch. A cancelled booking's email/SMS reminders can still be delivered because the cancellation calls are fire-and-forget and their failures are only console.logged, with no retry or DB marker when the request ends before they complete.

[BUG] Same unawaited-cancellation regression as handleCancelBooking: the reschedule handler drops the awaited Promise.all over reminder deletions, making all reminder cancels fire-and-forget. Rescheduling can complete while old-booking reminder cancellations are still in flight; a frozen serverless process abandons them and attendees receive reminders for the old, superseded booking time.

[BUG] The immediateDelete=true path cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes or marks the WorkflowReminder row, so callers in handleNewBooking.ts (reschedule), workflows.tsx deleteWorkflow, and the deleted-step branch leave rows in the DB with scheduled=true and cancelled=null. Orphaned reminder rows accumulate on every reschedule; if the SendGrid cancel API call fails (swallowed by console.log), the reminder is still sent and the DB row can never be reconciled because the cron's remindersToCancel query only selects cancelled:true.

[BUG] The updateEventTypes branch deletes the ownership-scoped deleteMany (which constrained deletion to `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }`) and replaces it with deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder, which delete the WorkflowReminder row by bare id with no user scoping. Reminder rows belonging to other users' bookings are deleted by id without the previous per-user authorization check that the removed prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany where-clause enforced.

[BUG] The condition `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` is narrowed to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, removing the custom-phone-number and verification UI for SMS steps that only require a sender ID — a behavioral UI change unrelated to the stated reminder-lifecycle intent. Users configuring sender-ID workflows lose access to the phone-number entry/verification flow this diff previously rendered, a regression bundled into a PR whose stated scope is booking-lifecycle reminder management.

[ADVISORY] A large whitespace-only re-indentation block (~60 lines in the SMS verification-code preview handler) is included in this diff with no functional change. Reviewers and git blame are burdened with noise unrelated to the reminder-management intent, and any real change hidden in that block is effectively unreviewable.

[ADVISORY] The cron's cancel loop awaits the SendGrid client.request serially per reminder inside a for-loop over remindersToCancel, and the outer try/catch aborts the whole batch on the first failure, skipping deletion of all subsequent already-cancelled reminders. A cron sweep with many due cancellations and one transient SendGrid error leaves the remaining rows marked cancelled but never deleted, requiring the next hourly sweep to redo the SendGrid cancel calls for reminders already cancelled.

[ADVISORY] The same EMAIL/SMS dispatch if/else over reminder.method is now copy-pasted across six call sites (handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx x3) with subtly inconsistent immediateDelete flags, replacing the previous single-source helper opportunity. The next reminder-method addition (e.g. a new channel) must be edited in six places, and the observed drift (immediateDelete true in some sites, absent in others) shows this is already diverging.

[BUG] remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => ...) fires deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder as unawaited promises, so the mutation returns before any cancellation or DB delete happens The previous code awaited ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany; the new async-fire-and-forget means on serverless/short-lived runtimes the process can terminate before the SendGrid/Twilio calls and prisma writes complete, leaving stale reminders that will still be delivered, plus unhandled promise rejections on failure

[BUG] Booking cancellation marks email reminders cancelled=true and relies on the hourly scheduleEmailReminders cron to actually cancel them, so a reminder already inside the SendGrid send window still fires after the booking is cancelled When a booking is cancelled shortly before its reminder time (or the cron last ran just before the cancellation), the next cron run can be up to a full hour away; the old code cancelled immediately via the SendGrid scheduled_sends API, so attendees now receive reminder emails for bookings that no longer exist — a user-visible regression from immediate to eventually-consistent cancellation

[BUG] The try/catch around the reminder-cancellation forEach can never catch anything because deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async and forEach does not await them, making the log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') handler dead code A failure in the SendGrid/Twilio cancellation (e.g. network error, expired API key) surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection instead of the intended logged-and-ignored error path, and the reschedule proceeds with old reminders still live; the same unawaited forEach pattern appears in handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings.tsx

[BUG] The cron's remindersToCancel findMany has no LIMIT/pagination (unbounded materialization on a recurring hot path) and issues one awaited sequential SendGrid API call per reminder inside the loop As cancelled reminders accumulate, each hourly cron run materializes every matching row into memory and makes N serial HTTP round-trips; one failed client.request aborts the whole loop via the catch, so the remaining reminders in the batch are neither cancelled via SendGrid nor deleted from the DB and will be retried as an ever-growing backlog

[BUG] The catch swallows the failure with console.log and the per-reminder prisma.workflowReminder.delete calls are collected into workflowRemindersToDelete but skipped entirely when any client.request throws A single SendGrid outage windows all DB cleanup: cancelled rows pile up, and on the next run the same failing reminder re-fails first, permanently starving the rest of the queue — a cascading-failure path with no per-item isolation or retry limit

[ADVISORY] SMS and EMAIL now follow divergent cancellation strategies in the same flow: SMS rows are hard-deleted immediately while EMAIL rows are soft-marked cancelled=true and only cleaned up later by the cron Cancelled email reminder rows accumulate in WorkflowReminder indefinitely (reminders whose scheduledDate has already passed never match the cron's lte now+1h window and are never deleted), and every consumer of booking.workflowReminders must now reason about two row lifecycles for the same concept

[ADVISORY] The new cancelled column is nullable Boolean, giving three representable states (null, false, true) for what is conceptually one flag, with no CHECK or default constraining it Callers must handle null-vs-false everywhere cancelled is read (e.g. the cron's cancelled:true filter silently excludes null rows), and nothing prevents the ambiguous state cancelled=true on a scheduled=false reminder; a NOT NULL DEFAULT false column would collapse the state space

[ADVISORY] deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels via the SendGrid API but neither deletes the row nor sets cancelled=true, leaving a scheduled=true, cancelled=null row that no later path cleans up unless a DB cascade removes it In the deleteWorkflow and deleted-step paths (workflows.tsx immediateDelete=true call sites), whether the orphaned row disappears depends entirely on the WorkflowStep onDelete: Cascade relation; any caller reaching this function without an enclosing cascade leaves a permanently 'scheduled' phantom row that future queries over workflowReminders will keep returning

[ADVISORY] In the step-update path, edited-step reminders are soft-cancelled (cancelled=true, scheduled stays true) while the same handler immediately schedules replacement reminders for the same bookings Until the hourly cron fires, a booking holds both an old (to-be-cancelled) and a new reminder row for the same step; any consumer iterating workflowReminders to count or display pending reminders sees duplicates, and a second edit in the same hour re-processes the already-cancelled rows since nothing filters cancelled=true from remindersFromStep

[BUG] The review iteration silently changed cancellation semantics from immediate SendGrid/Twilio cancellation+row deletion to a deferred cancelled-flag scheme, so a reminder scheduled within the next hour can still fire after the user cancelled the booking (cron only cancels at its next run). A user cancels a booking with a reminder 20 minutes out; the reminder is only marked cancelled=true in the DB and SendGrid batch is not cancelled until the hourly scheduleEmailReminders cron runs, so the attendee can still receive a reminder for a cancelled booking — a user-visible regression from the previous immediate-cancel behavior that no explicit human decision accepted.

[BUG] The diff silently drops the isSenderIdNeeded branch from the render condition, removing the sender-ID input UI for steps that require it — an unrelated scope change bundled into a reminder-cancellation PR. Users editing an SMS step that needs a sender ID no longer see the sender-ID field, so existing workflows referencing senderId become uneditable/unverifiable in the UI; this objective change was never declared in the PR intent and may be an accidental leftover from an intermediate iteration.

[BUG] The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row, leaving scheduled rows permanently in the DB with scheduled=true and cancelled=null. Every reschedule (handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true) and workflow deletion/edit leaves orphaned scheduled=true rows; the scheduleEmailReminders cron never re-processes them (they are not cancelled=true), so they are dead rows that accumulate indefinitely and any future query keyed on scheduled=true over-counts live reminders.

[ADVISORY] The cron now performs a full-table scan query on cancelled=true plus a sequential per-reminder SendGrid HTTP call inside the request handler, an unconditional hot-path cost added to an endpoint that previously only scheduled reminders. As cancelled rows accumulate (they are only deleted within the 1-hour window), every cron invocation queries an unbounded set and issues serial SendGrid requests, degrading the reminder scheduler latency for all tenants; the deferred-cancel design created this new workload without flagging it.

[ADVISORY] The cancelled-reminder query does not filter on scheduled or a non-null referenceId, so unscheduled or referenceId-less cancelled rows are fed to the SendGrid cancel call with batch_id: null. Rows marked cancelled before scheduling (e.g., via the non-immediate delete path on unscheduled reminders in workflows.tsx edit) hit the SendGrid cancel endpoint with a null batch_id, throwing errors that are swallowed by console.log while the surrounding try block also skips deletion of the remaining batch entries after Promise.all, leaving rows stuck.

[ADVISORY] deleteScheduledEmailReminder now has three divergent behaviors selected by a boolean flag plus a null-check (delete row / cancel-and-keep-row / mark-cancelled), with callers inconsistently choosing immediateDelete=true (workflow delete, step delete, reschedule) versus false (booking cancel, workflow edit), making the intended cancellation contract ambiguous. The next contributor extending cancellation (e.g., a new lifecycle event) must reverse-engineer which of three semantics applies from scattered call sites; the flag-trio-like split is why reschedule cancels immediately while booking-cancel defers, an inconsistency that will propagate.

[ADVISORY] SMS cancellation uses immediate deletion while EMAIL cancellation uses the deferred cancelled-flag scheme in the same call sites, so the two reminder methods no longer share a lifecycle contract. For a cancelled booking, the SMS row is deleted but the email row lingers as cancelled=true until the hourly cron deletes it; any code or reporting assuming both rows disappear together (or counting scheduled reminders per booking) observes divergent state between methods after the same user action.

[ADVISORY] The final hunk is pure whitespace/indentation mangling of previously correctly indented code plus removal of a commented-out BookingInfo import — unrelated churn smuggled into the diff. The mangled indentation (statements de-indented to column 0 inside nested blocks) makes future diffs and blame noisier and signals the block was reformatted by tooling without review; reviewers auditing intent cannot distinguish behavioral from cosmetic change here, increasing review cost on the next change to this function.

[ADVISORY] The update mutation's reminder deletion lost its ownership scope: the old code deleted via deleteMany with `where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } }`, while the new code calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder with the raw reminder.id and no userId constraint. Defense-in-depth against cross-tenant deletion is removed; correctness now depends entirely on the upstream reminder fetch being correctly scoped. Any future drift in that fetch (e.g., a team-workflow query joining bookings owned by other members) turns into a cross-user destructive write on workflowReminder rows with no server-side guard, and the deletion path now also fires external SendGrid/Twilio cancels for rows the acting user may not own.

[BUG] When immediateDelete=true the reminder is cancelled at SendGrid but its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so the row stays scheduled=true/cancelled=false forever. Reschedules (handleNewBooking.ts:964-968) and workflow/step deletions (workflows.tsx:211, 518) use immediateDelete=true; the orphaned rows are never picked up by the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only processes cancelled=true rows) and on every subsequent reschedule of the same booking they are re-sent to SendGrid's already-cancelled batch_id, producing swallowed errors and unbounded accumulation of dead reminder rows.

[BUG] twilio.cancelSMS throws for messages that are no longer queued (already sent/failed), and the wrapped prisma.workflowReminder.delete is then skipped by the catch, so the reminder row is never removed. Old bookings' SMS reminder rows whose Twilio SID is past the cancellable state permanently survive cancellation; every subsequent reschedule/cancel of that booking retries the failing Twilio call and the rows accumulate with no cleanup path, unlike the email path which marks rows cancelled for cron cleanup.

[ADVISORY] The cancellation sweep only picks up cancelled=true reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour, so correctness depends on this cron endpoint being invoked at least every hour. Self-hosted deployments configure their own cron cadence for this endpoint; any deployment invoking it less frequently than hourly will send cancellation emails for bookings that users explicitly cancelled, directly breaking the guarantee this PR claims to provide. The dependency is implicit and undocumented.

[ADVISORY] If the SendGrid cancel POST throws for one reminder, the catch aborts the loop and the already-collected prisma delete promises are never awaited, leaving those rows cancelled=true; the next cron run re-issues a POST cancel for the same batch_id, which SendGrid rejects for an already-cancelled batch, so the rows can cycle without ever being deleted. Reminder rows whose SendGrid cancellation succeeded on the first pass but whose delete raced a later reminder's failure can get stuck in a retry loop where every cron run errors on the duplicate cancel and never reaches the delete, leaving permanent stale rows.

[BUG] The try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting, so any rejection from those async calls occurs after the catch block has already passed and is never caught. The catch's log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') can only fire on a synchronous throw; real async failures (Sendgrid/Twilio errors, Prisma errors) propagate as unhandled promise rejections and are not logged by this handler, while the reschedule proceeds as if cancellation succeeded — stale reminders may still fire with no error surfaced.

[BUG] Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async but neither awaited nor collected into prismaPromises, so the cancel-booking API resolves success before (or despite failure of) the reminder cancellation. If twilio.cancelSMS or the Sendgrid cancel fails, the error is only console.log'd inside the manager, the booking is still reported cancelled, and the attendee receives an SMS/email reminder for a booking that no longer exists — user-facing failure that is invisible to both caller and user.

[BUG] The old code awaited Promise.all of the reminder deletions; the new code invokes the async delete functions in a forEach without awaiting, so the reschedule mutation returns success while cancellation is still in flight or has failed. A failed Twilio/Sendgrid cancel during reschedule is swallowed by console.log inside the manager; the previous booking's reminders fire even though the mutation reported success, and there is no error result or retry path.

[BUG] remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => ...) launches unawaited async callbacks, so the workflow update mutation resolves before any reminder cancellation completes and no rejection is ever observed. Edited-step reminders may keep firing after the user saved the workflow edit; failures are silently logged inside the manager and the API response reports success regardless, desyncing persisted 'cancelled' state from the user's expectation.

[BUG] deleteWorkflow fires reminder cancellation (including immediateDelete=true Sendgrid calls and Twilio cancels) without awaiting, so the deletion mutation returns success while remote cancellation is unresolved. Deleting a workflow reports success while scheduled SMS/emails may still be delivered; failures are only console.log'd with no surface to the caller.

[BUG] A single throw inside the per-reminder loop (e.g. a reminder with null referenceId sent as batch_id, or any Sendgrid error) aborts all remaining iterations and skips the entire Promise.all of deletes, with the whole failure reduced to console.log. One poisoned reminder row (referenceId null) permanently blocks cancellation and deletion of every other due reminder: the cron repeatedly fails on the same row, all other cancelled reminders within the hour window still fire to users, and nothing but a server log indicates the failure.

[BUG] The cron issues one sequential Sendgrid HTTP request per cancelled reminder with no timeout, batch cap, or pagination on the findMany, so a large backlog of cancelled reminders produces an unbounded, serial, timeout-less request burst on every cron tick. With a large cancelled backlog the cron run stalls indefinitely on a hung Sendgrid connection (no timeout configured), the tick overruns and the unscheduled-reminder scheduling below never runs, delaying all new reminders.

[BUG] All failures in deleteScheduledEmailReminder (Sendgrid cancel, Prisma update/delete) are swallowed into console.log, so callers that do await it (e.g. the immediateDelete path) still receive success. On the immediateDelete path used by workflow deletion and step deletion, a failed Sendgrid cancel leaves the batch still scheduled at Sendgrid while the local row was deleted on a subsequent path or the caller believes cancellation succeeded — the reminder fires with no record left to retry from.

[ADVISORY] The Sendgrid cancel-then-delete pair is not atomic: the request succeeds but the prisma.workflowReminder.delete can fail, and conversely the delete promises are only executed after the entire loop, so a crash mid-run re-cancels already-cancelled batches on the next tick. Operators debugging duplicate/no-op cron work see repeated redundant Sendgrid cancel POSTs for the same batch_id; harmless but noisy and hides real failures among repeated ones.

[ADVISORY] The non-immediate EMAIL path only sets cancelled=true and relies on the cron picking it up within the next hour, but the manager's contract (name 'deleteScheduledEmailReminder') no longer matches behavior — for reminders >1h away nothing is sent to Sendgrid until the cron window. Anyone adding a new call site assuming 'delete' means the remote send is cancelled immediately will introduce reminders that fire up to an hour after cancellation; the delayed semantics are implicit in the cron's 1-hour window and documented nowhere in this diff.

The diff also removed the prior Prisma `deleteMany` cleanup in multiple callers (e.g., `handleNewBooking.ts` uses `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`; `workflows.tsx` uses the `true` flag for deleted workflows/steps). It then processes them with a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) }`, which performs SendGrid cancellations sequentially (N serial HTTP calls). The entire loop and subsequent deletion scheduling are wrapped in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }`, so one thrown error from `client.request` aborts the remaining reminders; any not-yet-processed reminders are neither cancelled nor deleted and will be retried, potentially creating a growing backlog. This behavior is directly shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch swallows the failure with console.log and the per-reminder prisma.workflowReminder.delete calls are collected into workflowRemindersToDelete but skipped entirely when any client.request throws A single SendGrid outage windows all DB cleanup: cancelled rows pile up, and on the next run the same failing reminder re-fails first, permanently starving the rest of the queue — a cascading-failure path with no per-item isolation or retry limit

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation/deletion is wrapped in a single `try` with a sequential `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` that does `await client.request(...)` before enqueueing `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` and only `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop. If any `client.request` throws, control jumps to the `catch` (which only `console.log`s) and the already-collected Prisma deletes are never awaited/executed, leaving cancelled reminders in the DB. Because the next run queries the same `cancelled: true` reminders again and processes them sequentially, a consistently failing reminder can repeatedly abort the loop and block cleanup of subsequent items (starvation/cascading failure).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SMS and EMAIL now follow divergent cancellation strategies in the same flow: SMS rows are hard-deleted immediately while EMAIL rows are soft-marked cancelled=true and only cleaned up later by the cron Cancelled email reminder rows accumulate in WorkflowReminder indefinitely (reminders whose scheduledDate has already passed never match the cron's lte now+1h window and are never deleted), and every consumer of booking.workflowReminders must now reason about two row lifecycles for the same concept

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does introduce divergent cancellation lifecycles: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` always hard-deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row (and cancels Twilio if `referenceId` exists), while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` typically *does not delete* and instead sets `cancelled: true` (unless `referenceId` is null, or `immediateDelete` is true). Call sites like `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, and `workflows.tsx` now use these differing behaviors in the same conceptual “cancel reminders” flow.

However, the finding’s claim that cancelled email reminder rows "accumulate indefinitely" due to the cron filter is not supported: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` deletes rows where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, which includes reminders whose scheduledDate is already in the past (still `<= now+1h`). So the accumulation argument is incorrect as stated, but the inconsistency/maintenance concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new cancelled column is nullable Boolean, giving three representable states (null, false, true) for what is conceptually one flag, with no CHECK or default constraining it Callers must handle null-vs-false everywhere cancelled is read (e.g. the cron's cancelled:true filter silently excludes null rows), and nothing prevents the ambiguous state cancelled=true on a scheduled=false reminder; a NOT NULL DEFAULT false column would collapse the state space
matched_golden_ids: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that `cancelled` is a nullable Boolean, creating a problematic tri-state (null/false/true) where a simple flag is intended, and notes that null rows can be mishandled (e.g., filters excluding null) and that a NOT NULL DEFAULT false would prevent incorrect behavior. This matches the golden concern about null existing records and incorrect cancellation checks.

The diff shows multiple `immediateDelete=true` call sites (e.g., `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule cleanup and `workflows.tsx` deleted-workflow/deleted-step paths), so unless an external cascade happens, the row can persist as a phantom reminder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In the step-update path, edited-step reminders are soft-cancelled (cancelled=true, scheduled stays true) while the same handler immediately schedules replacement reminders for the same bookings Until the hourly cron fires, a booking holds both an old (to-be-cancelled) and a new reminder row for the same step; any consumer iterating workflowReminders to count or display pending reminders sees duplicates, and a second edit in the same hour re-processes the already-cancelled rows since nothing filters cancelled=true from remindersFromStep

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation to a soft-cancel by setting `cancelled: true` without deleting the row when `immediateDelete` is not passed (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })`). In the step-edit path shown (`workflowsRouter`, `remindersToUpdate.forEach`), email reminders are cancelled via `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (no `immediateDelete`), so the old reminder rows remain in the DB until the hourly `scheduleEmailReminders` job later finds `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour and deletes them. The finding’s downstream impact (duplicate reminders being shown/processed because queries don’t filter `cancelled=true`) is a plausible product/UX/data-model concern grounded in this new soft-cancel behavior, but the diff does not show the relevant `remindersFromStep` query or any consumer logic that counts/displays reminders, so the “verifiable defect” claim can’t be fully confirmed from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The review iteration silently changed cancellation semantics from immediate SendGrid/Twilio cancellation+row deletion to a deferred cancelled-flag scheme, so a reminder scheduled within the next hour can still fire after the user cancelled the booking (cron only cancels at its next run). A user cancels a booking with a reminder 20 minutes out; the reminder is only marked cancelled=true in the DB and SendGrid batch is not cancelled until the hourly scheduleEmailReminders cron runs, so the attendee can still receive a reminder for a cancelled booking — a user-visible regression from the previous immediate-cancel behavior that no explicit human decision accepted.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a real semantic change for EMAIL reminder cancellation: most call sites (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts and viewer/bookings.tsx) now call deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) without the new immediateDelete flag. In emailReminderManager.ts, when immediateDelete is falsy and referenceId exists, it does NOT cancel the SendGrid scheduled send; it only updates the DB row to { cancelled: true }. Actual SendGrid cancellation now happens later in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, which queries cancelled=true reminders within the next hour and then issues the cancel request + deletes the row. This creates a window where an already-scheduled SendGrid reminder may still send after the user cancels/reschedules, which is a user-visible regression from the prior behavior (immediate external cancel + DB deletion in the same flow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The immediateDelete path cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder row, leaving scheduled rows permanently in the DB with scheduled=true and cancelled=null. Every reschedule (handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true) and workflow deletion/edit leaves orphaned scheduled=true rows; the scheduleEmailReminders cron never re-processes them (they are not cancelled=true), so they are dead rows that accumulate indefinitely and any future query keyed on scheduled=true over-counts live reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early on the `immediateDelete` branch after cancelling the SendGrid batch (`POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends`), without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled=true`. Call sites in the diff pass `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule and `workflows.tsx` workflow/step deletion), so those reminders will remain in DB (likely still `scheduled=true` and `cancelled` null). The new cron logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only cleans up rows where `cancelled: true`, so these rows won’t be picked up for deletion, becoming orphaned/accumulating rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cron now performs a full-table scan query on cancelled=true plus a sequential per-reminder SendGrid HTTP call inside the request handler, an unconditional hot-path cost added to an endpoint that previously only scheduled reminders. As cancelled rows accumulate (they are only deleted within the 1-hour window), every cron invocation queries an unbounded set and issues serial SendGrid requests, degrading the reminder scheduler latency for all tenants; the deferred-cancel design created this new workload without flagging it.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the handler now does an extra `findMany` on `workflowReminder` for `{ cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() } }` and then iterates with a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) }`, i.e., serial SendGrid cancel calls inside the request handler. Because `lte now+1h` includes all past `scheduledDate` values, this can grow with accumulated cancelled reminders (not just “next hour”), adding unbounded/per-tenant workload to an endpoint that previously only scheduled reminders. This is a diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cancelled-reminder query does not filter on scheduled or a non-null referenceId, so unscheduled or referenceId-less cancelled rows are fed to the SendGrid cancel call with batch_id: null. Rows marked cancelled before scheduling (e.g., via the non-immediate delete path on unscheduled reminders in workflows.tsx edit) hit the SendGrid cancel endpoint with a null batch_id, throwing errors that are swallowed by console.log while the surrounding try block also skips deletion of the remaining batch entries after Promise.all, leaving rows stuck.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new `remindersToCancel` query filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= ...` and then unconditionally calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. Since `referenceId` is explicitly treated as nullable elsewhere (e.g. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId: string | null, ...)`), this code is not defensively constrained to `referenceId != null` (nor `scheduled: true`). However, the finding’s specific scenario (“rows marked cancelled before scheduling / referenceId-less cancelled rows caused by the non-immediate delete path”) is not supported by the diff because `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` deletes immediately when `referenceId` is null rather than setting `cancelled = true`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteScheduledEmailReminder now has three divergent behaviors selected by a boolean flag plus a null-check (delete row / cancel-and-keep-row / mark-cancelled), with callers inconsistently choosing immediateDelete=true (workflow delete, step delete, reschedule) versus false (booking cancel, workflow edit), making the intended cancellation contract ambiguous. The next contributor extending cancellation (e.g., a new lifecycle event) must reverse-engineer which of three semantics applies from scattered call sites; the flag-trio-like split is why reschedule cancels immediately while booking-cancel defers, an inconsistency that will propagate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now has three distinct code paths in `emailReminderManager.ts`: (1) if `referenceId` is null, it deletes the DB row; (2) if `immediateDelete` is true, it cancels the external scheduled send and returns without updating/deleting the DB row; (3) otherwise it only marks `cancelled: true` in the DB. Call sites choose `immediateDelete` inconsistently: e.g. reschedule and workflow/step deletion pass `true` (`handleNewBooking.ts`, `workflows.tsx`), while booking cancel / workflow edit paths call without the flag and thus just mark `cancelled` (`handleCancelBooking.ts`, `workflows.tsx`). This makes the cancellation semantics non-obvious and distributed across callers, matching the finding’s “ambiguous contract” concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SMS cancellation uses immediate deletion while EMAIL cancellation uses the deferred cancelled-flag scheme in the same call sites, so the two reminder methods no longer share a lifecycle contract. For a cancelled booking, the SMS row is deleted but the email row lingers as cancelled=true until the hourly cron deletes it; any code or reporting assuming both rows disappear together (or counting scheduled reminders per booking) observes divergent state between methods after the same user action.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an intentional divergence in cancellation semantics: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` always deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row via `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` (even if `referenceId` is null), while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` usually does NOT delete the row and instead sets `cancelled: true` (unless `referenceId` is null), relying on the new `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` hourly process to later cancel and delete rows with `cancelled: true`. Many call sites were updated to call email cancellation without `immediateDelete` (e.g., `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookings.tsx`, and parts of `workflows.tsx`), so after the same user action SMS rows disappear immediately but email rows persist flagged `cancelled`. This creates an inconsistent lifecycle that could affect any code/reporting that assumes both methods remove rows together, but the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual broken behavior elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update mutation's reminder deletion lost its ownership scope: the old code deleted via deleteMany with `where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } }`, while the new code calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder with the raw reminder.id and no userId constraint. Defense-in-depth against cross-tenant deletion is removed; correctness now depends entirely on the upstream reminder fetch being correctly scoped. Any future drift in that fetch (e.g., a team-workflow query joining bookings owned by other members) turns into a cross-user destructive write on workflowReminder rows with no server-side guard, and the deletion path now also fires external SendGrid/Twilio cancels for rows the acting user may not own.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an explicit ownership guard on deleting workflowReminder rows. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the old code performed `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` (defense-in-depth). The new code replaces this with calls to `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` which, per the diff, perform `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` (SMS) or `prisma.workflowReminder.delete/update({ where: { id: reminderId }})` (Email) with no `userId`/tenant constraint. That makes correctness/security rely entirely on the reminder fetch being properly scoped, and the finding’s concern about reduced defense-in-depth is grounded. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual cross-tenant deletion is possible today because we can’t fully verify the scoping of the upstream reminder queries from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When immediateDelete=true the reminder is cancelled at SendGrid but its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so the row stays scheduled=true/cancelled=false forever. Reschedules (handleNewBooking.ts:964-968) and workflow/step deletions (workflows.tsx:211, 518) use immediateDelete=true; the orphaned rows are never picked up by the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only processes cancelled=true rows) and on every subsequent reschedule of the same booking they are re-sent to SendGrid's already-cancelled batch_id, producing swallowed errors and unbounded accumulation of dead reminder rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after cancelling SendGrid (`POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends`), and it neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor marks it `cancelled=true` (no `prisma.workflowReminder.delete/update` in that branch). The diff shows multiple call sites using `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. `handleNewBooking.ts` reschedule cancellation and `workflows.tsx` workflow/step deletions), so those reminders will remain in the DB with `scheduled` unchanged and `cancelled` not set. The new cron logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` only picks up `cancelled: true` rows for cancellation/deletion, so these rows will never be cleaned up by that path, causing persistent/orphaned reminder rows and repeated attempts to cancel the same SendGrid `batch_id` on subsequent operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] twilio.cancelSMS throws for messages that are no longer queued (already sent/failed), and the wrapped prisma.workflowReminder.delete is then skipped by the catch, so the reminder row is never removed. Old bookings' SMS reminder rows whose Twilio SID is past the cancellable state permanently survive cancellation; every subsequent reschedule/cancel of that booking retries the failing Twilio call and the rows accumulate with no cleanup path, unlike the email path which marks rows cancelled for cron cleanup.

adjudication.rationale: In `smsReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` in a single `try/catch`. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws for any reason, execution jumps to the `catch` and the Prisma delete is skipped, leaving the reminder row in the DB. The diff also removed the separate Prisma `deleteMany` cleanup at call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, `viewer/workflows.tsx`), so there is no longer an independent deletion path. This can cause cancelled/rescheduled bookings to retain SMS reminder rows and repeatedly retry the failing Twilio cancel on subsequent operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cancellation sweep only picks up cancelled=true reminders whose scheduledDate is within the next hour, so correctness depends on this cron endpoint being invoked at least every hour. Self-hosted deployments configure their own cron cadence for this endpoint; any deployment invoking it less frequently than hourly will send cancellation emails for bookings that users explicitly cancelled, directly breaking the guarantee this PR claims to provide. The dependency is implicit and undocumented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation to be deferred: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now typically only sets `cancelled: true` in DB (unless `immediateDelete` is passed), instead of calling the provider cancellation API immediately. The actual provider-side cancel happens later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, but only for reminders where `cancelled: true` AND `scheduledDate <= dayjs().add(1, "hour")`. If this endpoint/cron runs less frequently than hourly, a reminder scheduled between runs (e.g., 90 minutes out) will not be cancelled in time and can still send despite the booking/workflow being cancelled/rescheduled. This correctness dependency is directly implied by the new 1-hour sweep window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] If the SendGrid cancel POST throws for one reminder, the catch aborts the loop and the already-collected prisma delete promises are never awaited, leaving those rows cancelled=true; the next cron run re-issues a POST cancel for the same batch_id, which SendGrid rejects for an already-cancelled batch, so the rows can cycle without ever being deleted. Reminder rows whose SendGrid cancellation succeeded on the first pass but whose delete raced a later reminder's failure can get stuck in a retry loop where every cron run errors on the duplicate cancel and never reaches the delete, leaving permanent stale rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block wraps the entire loop + `Promise.all` in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }`. Inside the loop it `await`s the SendGrid cancel request, then *collects* `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises in `workflowRemindersToDelete`, and only after the loop does it `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If any `client.request(...)` throws for a later reminder, control jumps to `catch` and the already-collected delete promises are never awaited/executed, leaving previously-successfully-cancelled reminders in the DB (still matching the `cancelled: true` query on subsequent runs). This partial-failure behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach that calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting, so any rejection from those async calls occurs after the catch block has already passed and is never caught. The catch's log.error('Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders') can only fire on a synchronous throw; real async failures (Sendgrid/Twilio errors, Prisma errors) propagate as unhandled promise rejections and are not logged by this handler, while the reschedule proceeds as if cancellation succeeded — stale reminders may still fire with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the new cancellation block does `try { originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); }); } catch { ... }`. Both `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are `async` (return Promises), but their returned Promises are neither `await`ed nor collected. As a result, any rejection from Sendgrid/Twilio/Prisma inside those functions will occur asynchronously and will not be caught by the surrounding `try/catch`, so the `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders", error)` won’t run for real async failures and the handler continues as if cancellations succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget: deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async but neither awaited nor collected into prismaPromises, so the cancel-booking API resolves success before (or despite failure of) the reminder cancellation. If twilio.cancelSMS or the Sendgrid cancel fails, the error is only console.log'd inside the manager, the booking is still reported cancelled, and the attendee receives an SMS/email reminder for a booking that no longer exists — user-facing failure that is invisible to both caller and user.

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places changed by this diff, async reminder-cancellation functions are invoked without awaiting or collecting the returned promises. Examples: `handleCancelBooking.ts` now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` inside nested `forEach` loops and also removed the prior Prisma `deleteMany` promises from `prismaPromises`, so `await Promise.all(...)` no longer waits on reminder cancellation/deletion at all. Similarly `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` and `viewer/workflows.tsx` call these async functions inside `forEach` without `await`. This makes reminder cancellation effectively fire-and-forget and allows the API/mutation to complete before cancellations/deletions finish (or even if they fail), matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The old code awaited Promise.all of the reminder deletions; the new code invokes the async delete functions in a forEach without awaiting, so the reschedule mutation returns success while cancellation is still in flight or has failed. A failed Twilio/Sendgrid cancel during reschedule is swallowed by console.log inside the manager; the previous booking's reminders fire even though the mutation reported success, and there is no error result or retry path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes awaited Prisma deletion promises and replaces them with calls to async cancellation functions inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts` drops `remindersToDelete` and no longer includes reminders in `Promise.all`; `bookingsRouter` reschedule path removes `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` and just calls `deleteScheduled*Reminder(...)`). Additionally, both managers swallow failures via `catch { console.log(...) }` without rethrowing, so cancellation failures won’t surface to the caller, matching the finding’s claim that reminders could still fire even though the mutation reported success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => ...) launches unawaited async callbacks, so the workflow update mutation resolves before any reminder cancellation completes and no rejection is ever observed. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, reminder cancellations are triggered inside `scheduledReminders.forEach(...)` (and other similar `forEach` loops) by calling the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await` and without collecting the returned promises. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A single throw inside the per-reminder loop (e.g. a reminder with null referenceId sent as batch_id, or any Sendgrid error) aborts all remaining iterations and skips the entire Promise.all of deletes, with the whole failure reduced to console.log. One poisoned reminder row (referenceId null) permanently blocks cancellation and deletion of every other due reminder: the cron repeatedly fails on the same row, all other cancelled reminders within the hour window still fire to users, and nothing but a server log indicates the failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block iterates `remindersToCancel` inside a single `try` and does `await client.request(...)` per reminder. Any thrown error (e.g., `reminder.referenceId` being `null` passed as `batch_id`, or a Sendgrid API failure) will immediately jump to `catch`, aborting the loop and skipping `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. Because there is no per-reminder error isolation and no `referenceId` null-check, one bad reminder can prevent processing/deleting the rest on every cron run, leaving other scheduled sends uncanceled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cron issues one sequential Sendgrid HTTP request per cancelled reminder with no timeout, batch cap, or pagination on the findMany, so a large backlog of cancelled reminders produces an unbounded, serial, timeout-less request burst on every cron tick. With a large cancelled backlog the cron run stalls indefinitely on a hung Sendgrid connection (no timeout configured), the tick overruns and the unscheduled-reminder scheduling below never runs, delaying all new reminders.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block does an unbounded `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` with no `take`/pagination, then iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and `await`s a SendGrid `client.request(...)` per reminder sequentially before proceeding to the later “find all unscheduled Email reminders” logic. If the result set is large, this cron handler can spend an arbitrarily long time in serial external HTTP calls and delay/skip scheduling of new reminders in the same run. The diff also does not show any per-request timeout or concurrency control around `client.request`, so a slow/hung request would block the whole handler.

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` wraps all logic in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and does not rethrow, so failures (Sendgrid cancel or Prisma ops in other branches) are silently ignored. On the `immediateDelete` path it attempts the Sendgrid cancel (`POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` with `status: "cancel"`) and then `return`s, meaning there is no DB-side "cancelled" marking or deletion within this function. Call sites use `immediateDelete` specifically when deleting workflows/steps (e.g. `workflowsRouter` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`), and deletions can cascade-delete `WorkflowReminder` rows (`WorkflowReminder.workflowStep` has `onDelete: Cascade`), so a failed Sendgrid cancel can leave the remote batch scheduled while the local reminder record is gone and the caller proceeds as if cancellation succeeded.
